resorts.name: Ski Portillo
resorts.notes: Operating for the 2026 season: multiple 2026 trade-press articles (Powder, FreeSkier, SnowBrains, Unofficial Networks, snowsportsnews) report Ski Portillo operating June 20 - Sept 26, 2026, following two consecutive above-average snow years. As of today (2026-07-12, mid-season) all 4 official webcams were fetched live/online, which is itself direct confirmation the resort is currently operating. Coordinates cross-checked: Wikipedia (32°50′10″S 70°07′44″W = -32.8361,-70.1289) vs latitude.to (-32.8370,-70.1289); averaged to -32.8367,-70.1289. resorts.name: Valle Nevado
resorts.notes:
Operating for 2026 season: opened June 19, 2026 (Vaivén chairlift first, other lifts phased in with snowfall), scheduled to run through Oct 4, 2026 conditions permitting. Now integrated with La Parva under the "Tres Valles" combined pass/mountain concept (with El Colorado planned to join), giving one of South America's largest lift-served domains (~1,700 ha, 87 runs, 30 lifts combined). $3.3M in 2026 capex: new Aconcagua Ski Residences (39 units), expanded snowmaking, lift/grooming upgrades. Sources: Teton Gravity Research, SnowBrains, Powder, WinterInsight (all June 2026).

Coordinates cross-checked: Wikipedia gives 33.356687°S, 70.249468°W; latitude.to gives -33.3547, -70.2498 (independent source, within ~250m — both plausible base-area points; used the Wikipedia value, rounded).

Elevation note/caution: Wikipedia's infobox "summit" figure of 5,430 m / 17,815 ft is NOT the resort's ski-lift summit — that number matches Cerro/Nevado El Plomo, a mountaineering peak (5,424–5,430 m) accessible from the resort but well above lift-served terrain. The actual ski-area summit, cross-checked independently on skimap.org and directly fetched from OnTheSnow, is 3,670 m / 12,041 ft, with base at 2,999–3,000 m / 9,843 ft (vertical drop ~810 m / 2,657–2,658 ft). Used the skimap.org/OnTheSnow figures as they describe the actual skiable summit, not a nearby mountaineering objective.

Webcams: Official site's /en/cameras/ page embeds 4 YouTube live streams (not static images or Vimeo/other iframe as sometimes seen at other Andes resorts). All 4 verified live via YouTube's oEmbed API and attributed to the official "Valle Nevado Ski Resort" YouTube channel (https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCeugwuttf3KGSyVuax_AzNw / @vallenevadoskiresort). No standalone static-image or link-only cams found beyond these 4.

Social links found in the official site's JSON-LD (Organization schema) at /en/cameras/: Facebook https://www.facebook.com/vallenevadoskiresort and X https://x.com/valle_nevado. Instagram (@valle_nevado, ~265K followers) confirmed via web search at https://www.instagram.com/valle_nevado/ — not independently fetched/verified live but URL/handle consistent with resort's other official branding (X handle also "valle_nevado").

resorts.name: Lagunillas
resorts.notes: Lagunillas (Centro de Ski Lagunillas) is Chile's only non-commercial ski center, founded and operated by Club Andino de Chile since 1933. Located in Cajón del Maipo, San José de Maipo commune, ~67 km/60 km SE of Santiago via Ruta G-25. Small area: 3 lifts, 13 runs, 200 hectares, night skiing offered. NO WEBCAM FOUND despite thorough checking: (1) official site skilagunillas.cl could not be reached directly by the fetch tool (connection refused on every attempt, both http/https) but was reachable via search-engine snippets/cache, and no webcam page appeared in any indexed subpage (checked schedule, routes, dining, norms, day-pass, season-pass-sales pages); (2) snow-forecast.com's dedicated webcam page for the resort explicitly states 'We don't have a live webcam for this resort'; (3) chilenieve.com's regional webcam roundup lists 8 other Chilean resorts but omits Lagunillas entirely; (4) no official YouTube live-stream channel found (only old promotional/tourist videos, e.g. a 2014 cinematic clip and 2024 vlogs - not live cams). Cams array is correctly empty per instructions. Elevation figures vary by source (base ~1896-2293m per snow-forecast/ioverlander vs. base 2200m/summit 2550m per skiresort.info and the resort's own '2,200m/7,200ft' marketing line) - I used skiresort.info's base/summit split (2200m/2550m, 350m vertical) since it's the only source giving both figures consistently and its 350m vertical roughly matches the ~305m (1000ft) vertical drop cited elsewhere. Coordinates cross-checked: ioverlander.com listing 'Ski center and cabins Lagunillas' gives -33.60710, -70.28884 (elev 2293m); snow-forecast.com independently gives 33.61°S, 70.28°W - close agreement, used the more precise ioverlander figure.

resorts.name: Nevados de Chillán
resorts.notes:
OPERATING STATUS: Operating for the 2026 season, but as of the research date (2026-07-12) is under a TEMPORARY weather closure. skiresort.info's live snow report (fetched 2026-07-12) shows current season dates "2026-06-29 - 2026-09-27" but status "Ski resort closed — Temporary" with 0 of 35km slopes / 0 of 16 lifts open due to conditions, base snow depth 0cm at time of check (5cm top/2400m). This matches the official site (nevadosdechillan.com homepage), which as of 2026-07-08 announced mountain activities (Parque Aventura + ski runs) suspended due to heavy rainfall, with the Adventure Park reopening 2026-07-11 (ski runs status not yet confirmed reopened). Earlier in the season (per press, July 3) the resort had reported 20cm base / 6 of 15 lifts open, so this is a storm-driven pause within an active season, not a season cancellation. Recommend a follow-up check closer to publish time given volatility.

ELEVATION: Cross-checked two sources — skiresort.info (base 1530m / summit 2400m, live snow-report page) and Spanish Wikipedia "Nevados de Chillán (centro de esquí)" (base 1540m / summit 2400m). Used 1530m/2400m (skiresort.info) → 5,020 ft base / 7,874 ft summit. Note: the volcanic summit itself (Nevados de Chillán volcanic complex, per English Wikipedia) is much higher at 3,212m/10,538ft — that is the mountain's true high point, not the ski area's lift-served summit (2400m), which is what's reported here per PeakCam convention (resort-served elevations).

COORDINATES: Cross-checked two sources for the ski-resort BASE AREA (not the volcano peak): (1) Spanish Wikipedia ski-resort article gives 36°54′33″S 71°25′08″O = -36.9092, -71.4189; (2) a web aggregator citation gives -36.903745, -71.409477. These two cluster within ~1.3 km of each other in the Valle Las Trancas / Termas de Chillán base area, so I used their midpoint (-36.9065, -71.4142). IMPORTANT: do not confuse with the volcanic-complex summit coordinates (-36.8633, -71.3767 per English Wikipedia / -36.858,-71.373 per latitude.to), which refer to the mountain peak ~5-6km away, not the ski base.

WEBCAMS: Official site's /camaras page (fetched raw HTML, since WebFetch's JS-rendering missed the iframes) embeds two ipcamlive.com live streams: "Novicios" (Pista Novicios) and "Plaza Tata". Both iframe URLs were curled directly and returned HTTP 200 with active ipcamlive player/stream tokens — confirmed live, not dead links. No YouTube live stream found: the resort's YouTube channel (youtube.com/channel/UCai0b2vM5thJK3Gt74rUupQ) exists and is linked in the footer, but the only embedded YouTube video discovered (via skiresort.info, id s9ZbR48rOYI) is a static 2021 promotional video ("Temporada Invierno 2021"), not a live cam — excluded. A third-party aggregator (vision-environnement.com) claims a Nevados de Chillán webcam but its direct image URL (https://www.vision-environnement.com/live/image/webcam/nevados-de-chillan.JPG) 302-redirected to the site's homepage rather than returning an image, so it was not included as a verified cam. OnTheSnow/snow-forecast/skiinfo/snow2day all appear to just be re-displaying the same two official Plaza Tata / Novicios cams rather than offering independent feeds.

OPERATING STATUS (2026): Best classified as "operating but not a traditional ski resort." Los Penitentes was closed for ~8 years after ~2016 due to financial/infrastructure collapse. Mendoza province re-tendered the concession; in July 2025 a 20-year concession was awarded to Mapsa Group S.A. (operator of Andes Truck, Villavicencio Park, Potrerillos Park), which rebranded operations as "Penitentes Park." As of July 2026 (current date), multiple Argentine outlets (infomendoza.info, June 8 2026; mendozaski.com; elsol.com.ar; sitioandino.com.ar; mdzol.com) confirm: it is NOT a fully operational lift-served ski center in 2026 — described explicitly as "sin centro de esquí operativo" / a "transition year" while the province negotiates a fuller long-term concession. It IS open daily 9am-5pm as a year-round "mountain recreational park": restaurant, bathrooms, parking, ski/snowboard rental, a ski school, and — key detail — the historic Pirca chairlift was mechanically restored and passed an INTI safety inspection, but as of July 2026 it is running for pedestrian/panoramic rides only, not full skier lift service. A search dated within the current season (La Nacion, "Llega el invierno," 20 June 2026) notes Mendoza resorts generally are contending with low natural snowfall in winter 2026, and a July-2026-dated result specifically says Penitentes has a restaurant/bathrooms running since early July but sledding/snow-play activities are suspended for lack of snow accumulation. Net: site is accessible and operating as a mountain park with a chairlift, but not delivering traditional downhill skiing this season — flag as "operating (limited/non-ski)" rather than a clean yes/no.

LOCATION: Km 1210 of National Route 7 (RN7), Las Heras department, Mendoza Province, Argentina — at the foot of Aconcagua, ~25 km from the Chile border (Paso Los Libertadores) and ~170-180 km from Mendoza City.
